verdict.rationale: Zep documents a prompt-ready Context Block that can be retrieved in one call. It comes from `thread.get_user_context()`, from `return_context=True` on `thread.add_messages()`, or from graph search with `scope="auto"`, which composes the most relevant edges, nodes, episodes, observations and thread summaries into a single ready-to-use block. Nothing in the evidence shows that the block can be capped to a caller-specified token budget, which is a named part of the story. Missing for 10: a documented token-budget or max-token parameter for the context block, and independent hands-on corroboration of context-block retrieval.

support.subject: As a developer, I can retrieve a token-budgeted, prompt-ready context block assembled from relevant memories in one call

citations.quote: set scope="auto" and let Zep dynamically compose the most relevant context across edges, nodes, episodes, observations, and thread summaries into a single ready-to-use block.
You can request the Context Block directly in the response to the `thread.add_messages()` call. This optimization eliminates the need for a separate `thread.get_user_context()` call.
Zep will perform a user graph search right after persisting the data and return the context relevant to the recently added messages.
